curriculum: NaCCA Religious and Moral Education Curriculum for Primary Schools, September 2019
accessibility_note: Teachers may read prompts aloud. Accept oral, written, drawn or role-play responses where suitable. Assess curriculum knowledge, not personal belief. Use teacher-provided accounts. No private religious disclosure or actual worship-site visits are required.

indicators.statement: Identify moral lessons learnt from responding to God’s call.

questions.prompt: A class account describes someone hearing God's call and faithfully carrying out a duty. Which quality does that action illustrate?
questions.hint: Look at how the person treated the duty.
questions.explanation: Following through on a duty demonstrates commitment.

questions.prompt: Which quality from the lesson is shown by a person who acts humbly and learns from others?
questions.hint: Think of the noun that goes with the word humble.
questions.explanation: Humility is shown when someone values others and does not boast.

questions.prompt: A person treats what is sacred with deep respect. Which term from the lesson describes this?
questions.hint: Think of an attitude towards what is sacred.
questions.explanation: Reverence means deep respect. The lesson includes reverence for God among its moral lessons.

questions.prompt: In a classroom story, Afia gives up part of her playtime to carry out a helpful promise. Which moral lesson could the class discuss? Use a detail.
questions.hint: What did Afia give up and what did she do instead?
questions.explanation: Giving up time for another person can illustrate sacrifice. Doing what she promised also illustrates commitment.

criteria.description: Names sacrifice, commitment or honouring promises.
Connects the quality to giving up playtime or keeping her word.

questions.prompt: The class has heard about the call of Moses, also called Musa. Name one moral lesson from the account and say which part suggests it.
questions.hint: Think of what Moses was asked and how he responded in the account.
questions.explanation: A learner might connect obedience to Moses responding to the call and explain that choice using the class account.

criteria.description: Names a lesson such as obedience, humility or commitment.
Links it to an action in the account the class heard.

questions.prompt: Draw a scene that illustrates respect as a moral lesson from responding to God's call. Give your picture a caption.
questions.hint: What could another person see or hear in the scene?
questions.explanation: A picture of people listening carefully can illustrate respect. The caption can name the action that shows it.

criteria.description: Depicts an observable respectful action.
Explains how the action expresses the named lesson.

questions.prompt: After a story about responding to God's call, Kofi says, “I see humility here.” Which detail would support his idea?
questions.hint: Look for the way the person treats others' ideas.
questions.explanation: Listening to advice without boasting shows humility.

questions.prompt: Choose respect or commitment. Explain how a pupil could practise it at school after a lesson about God's call.
questions.hint: Think about listening to others or finishing an agreed task.
questions.explanation: Respect might be shown by listening to a classmate. Commitment might be shown by carrying out an agreed classroom job.

criteria.description: Names the selected quality.
Gives a suitable school action and explains the link.

questions.prompt: Which action best illustrates honouring a promise in a class story?
questions.hint: Compare the action with what was agreed.
questions.explanation: The child returns the book as promised. Their action fits their word.
options: Hiding the book in a bag
Making a second promise and forgetting both
Blaming someone else for keeping it
Returning a borrowed book as agreed
questions.answer: Returning a borrowed book as agreed

questions.prompt: Act out a fictional scene about a learner responding to a call to help. Let a partner name the quality shown.
questions.hint: Choose an action that a classmate can recognise.
questions.explanation: A learner might put aside their own task briefly to help a partner. The scene can illustrate sacrifice or commitment.

criteria.description: Shows a clear action of service or cooperation.
Explains how the action illustrates one moral quality from the lesson.

questions.prompt: How might obedience be shown in an account about responding to God's call? Use an event in the account your class studied.
questions.hint: Find the instruction and what the person did next.
questions.explanation: Obedience can be shown by following the call. Connect the chosen account's instruction with the response it describes.

criteria.description: Identifies a safe and relevant response from the account.
Explains how following the call illustrates obedience.

questions.prompt: A pupil says the lesson is “commitment”. Which question helps them connect that idea with the account?
questions.hint: Which question asks for an action from the account?
questions.explanation: Evidence that someone continued to carry out a duty helps explain why commitment fits.
options: What did the person keep doing?
questions.answer: What did the person keep doing?

questions.prompt: Write two captions for a picture of a pupil doing an agreed classroom job. One should name an action. The other should name the moral lesson.
questions.hint: What happened, and what quality can we learn from it?
questions.explanation: “She returned the materials as agreed” describes an action. “She honoured her promise” identifies the lesson.

criteria.description: Gives a caption describing the action.
Links the action to commitment or honouring a promise.

questions.prompt: A partner suggests respect and you suggest humility after hearing the same account. How can you check whether both ideas fit?
questions.hint: Listen for evidence before deciding.
questions.explanation: The same response may show more than one quality. For each idea, name the action that supports it.

criteria.description: Identifies a relevant detail for each proposed quality.
Explains why both interpretations can fit or revises an unsupported idea.

questions.prompt: Make three cards showing a call, a response and a moral lesson in one account studied in class. Arrange them and explain the last card.
questions.hint: Choose what comes before the action and what can be learnt from it.
questions.explanation: The call gives the context, the response shows the action, and the lesson explains the quality shown.

criteria.description: Connects the response to the call in the account.
Names a moral quality that fits the response and gives a reason.

questions.prompt: A child says every promise is a sacrifice. Give an example of keeping a promise and explain what extra detail would show sacrifice.
questions.hint: Ask whether the person gave up time, effort or something else.
questions.explanation: Returning a pencil as agreed keeps a promise. Giving up playtime to finish a helpful duty could also show sacrifice.

criteria.description: Provides a clear kept promise.
Shows that sacrifice also involves giving up something valued.

questions.prompt: Make two panels about a classroom promise. Show it being made and then honoured. Explain the lesson that connects the panels.
questions.hint: Let a viewer see how the second picture relates to the first.
questions.explanation: A classmate may promise to return a book and then bring it back. The later action shows that the promise mattered.

criteria.description: Shows matching words and action in order.
Explains how the follow-through shows commitment or trustworthiness.

questions.prompt: Two narrators introduce a scene about a call and response. One names the event and one draws a moral lesson. Prepare both lines.
questions.hint: Which line tells what happened, and which explains what can be learnt?
questions.explanation: The first narrator identifies the call and response. The second explains what a quality such as obedience looks like in that event.

criteria.description: Accurately describes an event in the studied account.
Supports one moral interpretation with that event.

questions.prompt: A display gives only a person's name underneath the word “respect”. Improve it using an action from a class account and an explanation.
questions.hint: A name tells who. Add what that person did.
questions.explanation: A good display gives the reader an action to consider and explains why it illustrates respect.

criteria.description: Includes a relevant action from the account.
Explains how the action demonstrates respect.

questions.prompt: Choose a moral lesson from responding to God's call. Give one example from a class account and a different example from school life.
questions.hint: Use the same quality in two settings.
questions.explanation: A pupil might discuss commitment in responding to a call, then describe completing a classroom duty despite a distraction.

criteria.description: Connects the named lesson to an action in a class account.
Gives a different practical example of the same lesson at school.

indicators.content_standard: Appreciate the role of the family and the community in their relationship with God

skills.description: Recognise the examples and vocabulary in the lesson.
Explain meanings and connections in an example.
Apply the lesson to a situation and justify a choice.
Communicate understanding through a performance, drawing or demonstration.

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 foundational, 7 simple-use, 5 application and 3 challenge questions.

indicators.statement: Explain the need to live in harmony with one another.

questions.prompt: What does living in harmony with others mean?
options: Avoiding every person who is different
questions.hint: Think of how people can live well together.
questions.explanation: Harmony involves peaceful, respectful relationships.
questions.misconception_note: Harmony does not mean everyone must have identical beliefs.

questions.prompt: Name one reason it is important to live in harmony with others.
questions.hint: Think about what respectful relationships make possible.
questions.explanation: Harmony can benefit individuals and communities.
questions.misconception_note: Accept any reasonable explanation.

criteria.description: It can support peace, safety, cooperation, friendship or community wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour helps people live in harmony?
questions.hint: Choose a behaviour that supports peaceful communication.
questions.explanation: Listening helps people understand one another.
questions.misconception_note: Respectful listening allows disagreement.

questions.prompt: Two classmates disagree about a game rule. Which action best supports harmony?
options: Listen, explain calmly and agree on a fair solution
questions.answer: Listen, explain calmly and agree on a fair solution
questions.hint: Look for a peaceful and fair way to solve the disagreement.
questions.explanation: Calm discussion and fairness can resolve conflict.
questions.misconception_note: Harmony does not mean hiding a problem; it means addressing it respectfully.

questions.prompt: How can cooperation help a group live in harmony?
questions.hint: Think about what happens when people help one another.
questions.explanation: Cooperation strengthens relationships and shared work.
questions.misconception_note: Accept age-appropriate examples.

criteria.description: It helps members work together, share tasks and reach goals peacefully.

questions.prompt: State one way you can help maintain harmony in a classroom.
questions.hint: Think of a practical classroom action.
questions.explanation: Learners can contribute to respectful classroom relationships.
questions.misconception_note: No personal religious disclosure is required.

criteria.description: A constructive action such as listening, sharing fairly, using kind words or resolving disagreements calmly.

questions.prompt: Match the action with its effect: (1) sharing fairly; (2) listening carefully; (3) apologising after harm. Effects: A. helps repair a relationship; B. helps people feel heard; C. reduces conflict over resources.
questions.hint: Connect each action to a likely positive effect.
questions.explanation: Respectful actions can strengthen harmony.
questions.misconception_note: Accept equivalent descriptions of the effects.

criteria.description: Matches 1 with C.
Matches 2 with B.
Matches 3 with A.

questions.prompt: Why is it helpful to respect people whose beliefs differ from yours?
options: It supports peaceful relationships and fair treatment
It means you must agree with every belief
It gives permission to mock others
questions.answer: It supports peaceful relationships and fair treatment
questions.hint: Respect is about how we treat people.
questions.explanation: People can disagree while treating one another with respect.
questions.misconception_note: Respect is not the same as agreement.

questions.prompt: A new learner is left out of a group activity. What could classmates do to support harmony?
options: Invite the learner and share roles fairly
questions.answer: Invite the learner and share roles fairly
questions.hint: Choose an inclusive and fair action.
questions.explanation: Inclusion helps build a caring group.
questions.misconception_note: Do not assume anything about the learner's background.

questions.prompt: Draw a scene showing people living in harmony and label one action that helps them get along.
questions.hint: Show actions such as sharing, listening or helping.
questions.explanation: A drawing can represent ways people live peacefully together.
questions.misconception_note: Assess the idea, not artistic skill.

criteria.description: A clear scene showing respectful or cooperative behaviour with a suitable label or explanation.

questions.prompt: Which statement about harmony is true?
options: People can live peacefully while having different opinions
Disagreement must be solved by force
questions.answer: People can live peacefully while having different opinions
questions.hint: Harmony allows respectful differences.
questions.explanation: Peaceful relationships do not require identical views.
questions.misconception_note: Learners should not equate harmony with silence or conformity.

questions.prompt: Give one peaceful way to respond when someone has upset you.
questions.hint: Choose a response that does not harm or threaten anyone.
questions.explanation: Peaceful communication can help resolve conflict.
questions.misconception_note: If someone is unsafe, seeking a trusted adult is appropriate.

criteria.description: Speak calmly, explain the problem, listen, seek help or agree on a fair solution.

questions.prompt: A group must choose one activity, but members have different ideas. What is a harmonious way to decide?
options: Hear each idea and choose fairly, perhaps taking turns
Let the loudest person threaten others
questions.answer: Hear each idea and choose fairly, perhaps taking turns
questions.hint: Look for a fair process that lets people participate.
questions.explanation: Fair decision-making supports cooperation.
questions.misconception_note: A fair outcome may involve compromise or taking turns.

questions.prompt: What can happen when people use kind words and fair actions?
options: People lose the right to disagree
questions.hint: Think about how considerate behaviour affects relationships.
questions.explanation: Kindness and fairness can help build trust.
questions.misconception_note: Say “may” because outcomes are not guaranteed in every situation.

questions.prompt: In a small group, role-play a disagreement about sharing classroom materials and show a peaceful, fair solution.
questions.hint: Use calm words and include everyone involved.
questions.explanation: Role-play practises practical skills for living in harmony.
questions.misconception_note: Do not use insults or imitate a real classmate.

criteria.description: speaks and listens respectfully
solution is fair
group works together

questions.prompt: Match each value with a helpful action: (1) respect; (2) fairness; (3) cooperation. Actions: A. share turns equally; B. listen without mocking; C. work together on a task.
questions.hint: Match each value to an action that shows it.
questions.explanation: Values can be practised through everyday behaviour.
questions.misconception_note: Accept equivalent examples if asked orally.

criteria.description: Matches 1 with B.
Matches 2 with A.
Matches 3 with C.

questions.prompt: Explain one way harmony can help a family, school or community.
questions.hint: Choose one group and describe a benefit.
questions.explanation: Harmony can help groups work and live together.
questions.misconception_note: Accept responses from the learner's chosen setting without asking for private details.

criteria.description: A reasonable explanation such as improving safety, cooperation, friendship or shared problem-solving.

questions.prompt: Does living in harmony mean never disagreeing? Explain briefly.
questions.hint: Think about whether respectful disagreement is possible.
questions.explanation: Harmony is compatible with different opinions.
questions.misconception_note: Do not reward the idea that one person must always give in.

criteria.description: No. People may disagree and still treat one another peacefully and respectfully.

questions.prompt: Create a short oral explanation, written response or labelled drawing showing why harmony matters and one action that supports it.
questions.hint: Include one benefit and one example of respectful behaviour.
questions.explanation: This assesses understanding of the importance of harmony.
questions.misconception_note: Allow multiple valid reasons and accessible response modes.

criteria.description: explains a benefit
gives a practical supporting action
communicates clearly

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows the importance of living in harmony?
options: People can cooperate, solve problems peacefully and treat one another fairly
Everyone must follow one person's beliefs
Only people who agree can work together
questions.answer: People can cooperate, solve problems peacefully and treat one another fairly
questions.hint: Choose the inclusive, peaceful outcome.
questions.explanation: Harmony supports cooperation, fair treatment and peaceful problem-solving.
questions.misconception_note: Respect differences while maintaining safe, fair boundaries.

indicators.content_standard: Explain the role of the family members in living safely with each other
